title: Context menu contributions
summary: Context-menu actions are contributions registered against typed target families and described by plain data fields, so a menu can be drawn without loading the contributor's React component.
firstReason: Plain-data actions resolved for a typed target suit server rendering well: the host resolves the actions and renders the menu. The registration through client plugin slots is replaced; contributions come from Go components or plugin processes.

title: Replaceable product icons through an SVG sprite
summary: Each product icon is a symbol in one hidden SVG sprite and is drawn with `<use>`. A theme can replace the artwork, and replaced icons still follow the current colour and the light or dark palette.
firstReason: An SVG sprite is plain HTML and CSS, so it works unchanged in server-rendered templates and needs no JavaScript. It also keeps icon markup small in every rendered fragment.

title: Separate background Shell command display from job state
summary: The tool card of an explicit background `bash` or `pwsh` call shows the command and working directory in the ordinary shell layout. Once the launch is acknowledged the card becomes a static command display without a run-state dot or exit code, because the acknowledgement says nothing about the background job.
firstReason: The rule is about not misreporting job state from a launch acknowledgement, which any UI must honour. The Go host renders the card in a template from the same two facts (`background` and `running`); DH-ADR-3 changes only where it is rendered.

title: Spring-based edge recovery for floating dock panels
summary: Floating dock panels may be dragged past the viewport edge but spring back into a legal region when released, so a panel's header and resize corner can never be lost off screen. The rule lives in one shared gesture hook.
firstReason: The rule matters only if the Go UI keeps floating panels (see the docking note). If it does, the constraint that a floating panel can always be recovered lives inside that JavaScript island; if it does not, there is nothing to carry.
